sessions.phase_label: Initial visual direction and first-scene image development

requirements.title: Animated Trailer as Primary Deliverable
requirements.definition: Produce the project as an animated trailer before considering a still-frame alternative.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers selection of animation as the primary output; animation quality and the conditional digital-comic fallback can evolve independently.

requirements.title: Acceptable Animation Quality
requirements.definition: The animated output must achieve a level of motion and presentation quality acceptable to the client.
requirements.boundary_note: Animation quality can fail or require refinement independently of character look development and independently of whether animation remains the selected medium.

requirements.title: Digital Comic Fallback
requirements.definition: Use a digital comic composed of still frames only if animation produces inadequate results or becomes too difficult or expensive.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a conditional alternative deliverable rather than an attribute of the animated trailer and can remain inactive while animation proceeds.

requirements.title: Trailer Text Cards
requirements.definition: Text cards are excluded from the freelancer's trailer deliverable because the client will handle them separately.
requirements.boundary_note: Retained as an independent deliverable element even though the first visible evidence removes it from freelancer scope; no hidden introduction should be fabricated.

requirements.title: Full-Color Video
requirements.definition: Render the entire final video in color rather than using the storyboards' black-and-white presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Color treatment is independently configurable and testable from video orientation and artistic style.

requirements.title: Vertical 9:16 Aspect Ratio
requirements.definition: Format the final video vertically at a 9:16 aspect ratio.
requirements.boundary_note: Aspect ratio is a standalone output constraint and is not an attribute of color treatment or scene composition.

requirements.title: Artistic Style Consistency
requirements.definition: Maintain the intended artistic style consistently across generated trailer imagery without gradual stylistic drift.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers cross-project style stability; character-specific appearance and set-specific quality or continuity remain independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: Character Visual Style
requirements.definition: Render Q, Deadwax, and Nova with the requested character details and a rougher, darker, graffiti-like, sketch-energized visual style.
requirements.boundary_note: Reference-image combination, preferred detail level, and application to all three characters are attributes of one character-design mechanism; responsibility for producing references may change without changing the desired appearance.

requirements.title: Set Image Quality
requirements.definition: Use set imagery of sufficient visual quality, including newly generated set images when beneficial rather than remaining limited by inadequate source-image resolution.
requirements.boundary_note: Image quality can be improved independently of whether recurring set designs remain visually consistent between shots.

requirements.title: Set Visual Continuity
requirements.definition: Keep newly created set backgrounds aligned with the intended style and visually consistent from shot to shot.
requirements.boundary_note: Set continuity is judged separately from raw set-image resolution and from character appearance.

requirements.title: Accurate Shot Direction
requirements.definition: Render shots according to the current script and detailed shot direction, especially where the script intentionally differs from an older storyboard reel.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the acceptance behavior of matching current shot directions, not the administrative process for communicating revisions; independently specified scene compositions remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Opening Aerial Establishing Shot
requirements.definition: Include the opening aerial establishing shot as a lower-priority element after required material is completed.
requirements.boundary_note: The aerial shot has its own priority and deferment trajectory and can be omitted from the current phase while other shot-direction Requirements remain active.

requirements.title: CC1 Character Framing Sequence
requirements.definition: For the specified CC1 sequence, provide three pairs of Q and Deadwax images progressing from long or wide shots to mid shots and then waist-up closer shots.
requirements.boundary_note: The paired character count and wide-to-close progression form one tightly coupled scene mechanism rather than separate Requirements for each frame or distance.

requirements.title: Q Frame Bridge Composition
requirements.definition: Remove the obstructive lower bridges around Q so that only the designated upper bridge remains in the affected Q images.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a specific frame-composition correction that can be completed or judged independently of character shadows and broader set continuity.

requirements.title: Character Shadows in Revised Frames
requirements.definition: Restore the characters' shadows in the affected revised renders without otherwise changing those images.
requirements.boundary_note: Shadow presence has its own concrete failure and correction criterion and is separate from bridge removal and general artistic style.
